title: Built-in functions SQL Server has and Fabric rejects
summary: Fabric Warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint reject many SQL Server built-ins with 'not supported'. The main gaps are randomness (RAND, CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM, NEWSEQUENTIALID), identity retrieval (@@IDENTITY, SCOPE_IDENTITY, IDENT_CURRENT, IDENT_SEED, IDENT_INCR), part of error handling (ERROR_LINE, XACT_STATE, FORMATMESSAGE), session and login info (APP_NAME, HOST_NAME, ORIGINAL_LOGIN, USER_ID, SUSER_ID, SESSION_ID), encryption functions, and file or filegroup metadata. Use NEWID for randomness and unique ids, ROW_NUMBER for surrogate keys, and ERROR_NUMBER, ERROR_MESSAGE and @@TRANCOUNT in TRY...CATCH. Use @@SPID, SUSER_SNAME and USER_NAME for session and identity info. Error numbers are left open: the probe settles which 'not supported' code applies.

claims.statement: RAND is not supported. For a random integer, use ABS(CHECKSUM(NEWID())) with a modulo. It is evaluated per row, unlike RAND without a seed.
claims.sql_server: RAND() returns a float and is evaluated once per query when no seed is given.

claims.statement: The NEWID-based random integer compiles in Fabric and returns int.
CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM is not supported. For random bytes, cast NEWID to varbinary(16). This is not cryptographically strong.
claims.sql_server: CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM returns cryptographic random varbinary bytes.
claims.alternative: SELECT CAST(NEWID() AS varbinary(16)) AS b

claims.statement: NEWSEQUENTIALID is not supported. NEWID exists and returns uniqueidentifier, but its values are not ordered.
claims.sql_server: NEWSEQUENTIALID is only allowed in a DEFAULT constraint on a uniqueidentifier column.

claims.statement: SCOPE_IDENTITY, @@IDENTITY and IDENT_CURRENT are all not supported. Do not read back a generated key after an insert. Generate keys yourself, for example with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ...) added to the current MAX of the key.
claims.sql_server: SCOPE_IDENTITY returns the last identity value inserted in the current scope.
claims.alternative: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY v) AS id FROM (VALUES ('a'),('b')) AS t(v)

claims.statement: @@IDENTITY is not supported either. Rewriting SCOPE_IDENTITY to @@IDENTITY does not help.
claims.sql_server: @@IDENTITY returns the last identity value in the session across scopes.

claims.statement: IDENT_SEED and IDENT_INCR are not supported. You cannot inspect identity seed or increment metadata with them.

In TRY...CATCH, ERROR_LINE is not supported. ERROR_NUMBER, ERROR_MESSAGE, ERROR_SEVERITY, ERROR_STATE and ERROR_PROCEDURE exist. Copying a SQL Server CATCH block that logs ERROR_LINE makes the whole batch fail.
claims.sql_server: ERROR_LINE returns the line number where the error occurred.
claims.alternative: SELECT ERROR_NUMBER() AS n, ERROR_MESSAGE() AS m, ERROR_PROCEDURE() AS p

claims.statement: XACT_STATE is not supported. In a CATCH block, test @@TRANCOUNT > 0 before ROLLBACK instead.
claims.sql_server: XACT_STATE returns 1, 0 or -1 to signal a committable, absent or uncommittable transaction.

claims.statement: FORMATMESSAGE is not supported. Build error text with CONCAT before THROW.
claims.sql_server: FORMATMESSAGE formats a printf-style message string.

claims.statement: APP_NAME and HOST_NAME are not supported. For a session identifier, @@SPID exists.
claims.sql_server: APP_NAME returns the client application name and HOST_NAME the client workstation name.

claims.statement: SESSION_ID is not recognized as a built-in function. Use @@SPID.
ORIGINAL_LOGIN, SUSER_ID, USER_ID and DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID are not supported. For the caller's name, use SUSER_SNAME, USER_NAME, CURRENT_USER or SYSTEM_USER.
claims.sql_server: ORIGINAL_LOGIN returns the login that started the session, even after impersonation.

claims.statement: ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE, DECRYPTBYPASSPHRASE, ENCRYPTBYKEY, DECRYPTBYKEY and the certificate and asymmetric key variants are not supported. HASHBYTES exists for one-way hashing only; it is not a replacement for reversible encryption.
claims.sql_server: ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE returns varbinary ciphertext that DECRYPTBYPASSPHRASE can reverse.

claims.statement: File and filegroup metadata functions are not supported: FILE_ID, FILE_NAME, FILEPROPERTY, FILEGROUP_ID, FILEGROUP_NAME and FILEGROUPPROPERTY. Storage is managed by the service, and the list offers no alternative.
